cohort_name: PAFIP (Programa Asistencial Fases Iniciales de Psicosis), Cantabria
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV (APA, 2000) brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder; Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I)
diagnosis_confirmed: SCID-I administered by the same senior consultant psychiatrist six months after the baseline visit; diagnostic stability reviewed at the 10-year reassessment (ayesaarriola2020, Methods, Clinical and functional instruments, p. 6)
overlap_notes: Recruitment years are those of PAFIP-10 (referrals between February 2001 and December 2008, ayesaarriola2020, Methods, Study design and setting, p. 6). PAFIP itself is described as ongoing and mayoralvanson2019 does not state which years its 157-patient subsample covers, so its window may be narrower or wider. ayesaarriola2020 analyses 307 baseline and 209 reassessed patients; mayoralvanson2019 analyses 157. The overlap between the two analysed samples is not stated.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'The PAFIP-10 sample comprised all referrals to PAFIP between 2001 and 2008 that had been screened against the following inclusion criteria: age 15-60 years; living in the catchment area; experiencing their first episode of psychosis; no prior treatment with antipsychotic medication or, if previously treated, a total life time of adequate antipsychotic treatment of <6 weeks; meeting DSM-IV criteria (APA, 2000) for brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, or schizoaffective disorder. DSM-IV criteria for drug or alcohol dependence, intellectual disability, and having a history of neurological disease or head injury were exclusion criteria.' No criterion refers to employment, unemployment, wanting or being ready to work, an employment goal, vocational-service eligibility, a placement or previous employment failure. The programme is catchment-based: 'incidence and 10-year follow-up studies, respectively, of all individuals with an FEP presenting for the first time to mental health specialists in the catchment area of Cantabria'. Employment was measured at entry, not required: 69 of 156 were unemployed and 30 inactive at baseline (mayoralvanson2019, Table 3, p. 1186).
employment_selection_source: ayesaarriola2020, Methods, Subjects, p. 6, and Methods, Study design and setting, p. 6. mayoralvanson2019 does not restate the criteria: 'Both inclusion and exclusion criteria have also been described elsewhere (15)' (Methods 2.2 Subjects, p. 1183), so the cohort-level decision rests on ayesaarriola2020. The analysis-sample decision for mayoralvanson2019's 157 is recorded separately as analysis_selection_status = unclear in extraction_arms.

cohort_name: OnTrackNY coordinated specialty care programme, New York State
diagnostic_instrument: Clinician diagnosis of primary nonaffective psychosis with onset less than two years before enrolment; no structured research instrument
diagnosis_confirmed: 'Licensed team clinicians conducted a nonstandardized interview at intake. Because the goal of the interview was to establish a diagnosis of primary, nonaffective psychosis to determine eligibility, clinicians received training in differential diagnosis.' (nossel2018, Methods, Measures, p. 864). Diagnosis is programme-assigned and not independently verified.
overlap_notes: nossel2018 covers enrolments October 2013 to August 2016 at 10 sites (325 clients); basaraba2023 covers October 2013 to December 2018 at 20 sites (1298 clients) and therefore contains nossel2018's sample. Results from the two reports describe overlapping participants.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'The total sample included individuals ages 16 to 30 who had experienced nonaffective psychosis for less than two years, were enrolled at one of 10 OnTrackNY sites, and had completed at least one three-month follow-up assessment.' (nossel2018). 'The OnTrackNY program, a network of CSC sites in New York State, provides person-centered, recovery-oriented, and evidence-based psychosocial and pharmaceutical interventions to individuals aged 16 to 30 years with recent-onset (<2 years) nonaffective psychosis.' (basaraba2023). No eligibility criterion refers to employment status, wanting or readiness to work, an employment goal, vocational-service eligibility, a placement or previous employment failure; 56 per cent of the 325 were in neither work nor school at admission (nossel2018, Table 1, p. 865) and were retained. NOTE AS PROVENANCE, NOT SELECTION: the OnTrackNY service model itself includes 'a supported education and employment specialist' on every team, so care received is employment-supporting; entry to the service is not conditional on any employment criterion.
employment_selection_source: nossel2018, Methods, Participants and Study Design, p. 864, and Intervention, p. 864; corroborated by basaraba2023, Design Setting and Participants, p. 49, and Introduction, p. 50.

cohort_name: US Veterans Health Administration schizophrenia cohort (VHA Corporate Data Warehouse, 2013-2019)
diagnostic_instrument: Two or more administrative diagnosis records on different days: ICD-9-CM 295.xx, ICD-10-CM F20.x, F21 or F25.x, in any position
diagnosis_confirmed: Administrative diagnosis codes only; no clinical interview, chart review or validation of the codes is reported in either report.
overlap_notes: One source cohort of 119,343 veterans, reported twice. lin2022 propensity-matches 102,207 of them to non-schizophrenia veterans; benson2022 splits the same 119,343 into 16,866 with and 102,477 without a relapse in the 12-month pre-index period and propensity-matches 16,862 from each. The analysed samples of the two reports overlap by an unquantified but large amount and are not independent.
employment_selection_verbatim: Selection is given in full as a flow chart in both reports and contains no employment-related step: 'two or more records on different days with a diagnosis for schizophrenia (ICD-9-CM: 295.xx; ICD-10-CM: F20.x, F21, F25.x) in any position during the study period (January 1, 2013-September 30, 2019)'; 'one or more record with a diagnosis for schizophrenia in any position during the patient selection window (January 1, 2014-September 30, 2019)'; 'Enrolled in VHA benefits for minimum of 12 months prior to the index date'; 'one or more record (any medical and pharmacy benefit record) during the 12-month preindex period and at any time after the index date'; plus, in lin2022, 'Age >=18 years on the index date' and 'No missing data for age, gender, or region; region not outside the US; no other data quality issues'. Employment status is an outcome obtained by record linkage, not an entry criterion.
employment_selection_source: benson2022, Figure 1 'Patient Selection Criteria Flowchart' (PDF p. 6) and Methods, Study Design; lin2022, Figure 1 'Patient selection criteria and attrition', p. 3, and Methods, Study design, p. 3.
